If you’re studying Computer Science or Quantitative Stats, you’ve likely felt the sting of a lower-than-expected grade despite the code 'running perfectly.' 

Markers aren't just looking for functionality—they are looking for academic rigor and clarity. 

THE 54% TRAP: Submitting raw code with zero comments, or pasting raw SPSS output tables into a dissertation without reporting degrees of freedom, p-values, or effect sizes. This signals to your marker that you haven't engaged with the underlying logic.

THE 1ST CLASS BLUEPRINT: Production-grade code with modular architecture and Big-O proofs, combined with professional APA 7th statistical write-ups of regression models. When you frame your data through the lens of academic theory, your work moves from 'functional' to 'exceptional.'
